comments.body:
**Not a defect in this repository — the failing check is running against an ESP-IDF v6.1 Python environment**

`M5Cardputer-UserDemo` declares **ESP-IDF v4.4.6** (`README.md:14`, `dependencies.lock:18`), and it contains no `install.sh` and no Python build-requirements file. The `install.sh` in play is ESP-IDF's own, and the check that fails is `$IDF_PATH/tools/check_python_dependencies.py`. `rich-click~=1.9.0` appears in neither this project nor ESP-IDF 4.4.6 (which only requires `click>=7.0`); it is an **ESP-IDF v6.1** constraint (`espidf.constraints.v6.1.txt:8`, https://dl.espressif.com/dl/esp-idf/espidf.constraints.v6.1.txt). So the environment being checked is a 6.1 environment, not the 4.4.6 toolchain this project is built with.

What the two lines actually mean:

1. `rich-click 1.8.9` vs `~=1.9.0`: the environment still has the version installed by an older IDF, i.e. `install.sh` did not update *this* environment.
2. `No package metadata was found for bitarray` is the real failure. `bitarray` arrives through esptool → `bitstring` (pinned `<5` in the 6.1 constraints) → `bitarray`; its `.dist-info` metadata is missing while the module directory can still be present, so `importlib.metadata` cannot see it. Re-running the checker cannot repair that.

The changing name in "a different package goes missing" is a checker artifact, not changing damage: the handler at `tools/check_python_dependencies.py:176` prints `req` left over from the loop at line 135, and the requirement order comes from a set, so the printed name differs per process. The package after the colon (`bitarray`) is the one that actually fails.

**Evidence level: host-level test + code-level verification.** With IDF v6.1's own checker I reproduced both lines on the host: a clean 6.1 environment passes; after `pip install rich-click==1.8.9` it reports the version mismatch; after removing only `bitarray`'s `dist-info` it reports `No package metadata was found for bitarray`, with the leading name varying between `packaging`, `bitstring` and `rich-click~=1.9.0` across 18 runs — one run is byte-identical to yours. Virtual-device/hardware validation does not apply: the failure happens before any firmware exists.

**Fix** — rebuild the environment instead of re-running `install.sh` over it, and use the IDF this project declares:

```bash
# 1) show which toolchain is really in use
idf.py --version
echo "$IDF_PATH"; git -C "$IDF_PATH" rev-parse --short HEAD
echo "$IDF_PYTHON_ENV_PATH"; command -v python; python -V

# 2) remove exactly the env printed above (guarded)
[ -n "${IDF_PYTHON_ENV_PATH:-}" ] && case "$IDF_PYTHON_ENV_PATH" in */python_env/*) rm -rf "$IDF_PYTHON_ENV_PATH";; esac

# 3) reinstall from the same checkout and re-check
cd "$IDF_PATH" && ./install.sh esp32s3      # install.bat on Windows
. ./export.sh
python -c "import importlib.metadata as m; print(m.version('rich-click'), m.version('bitarray'))"
```

For this repository, use v4.4.6:

```bash
git clone -b v4.4.6 --recursive https://github.com/espressif/esp-idf.git ~/esp/esp-idf-v4.4.6
cd ~/esp/esp-idf-v4.4.6 && ./install.sh esp32s3 && . ./export.sh
cd /path/to/M5Cardputer-UserDemo && idf.py build
```

**Not covered**: I did not build this project with v6.1 (not the declared toolchain, so further 6.1 errors would be a separate issue), and I did not build with v4.4.6 either — this reply only explains the Python check. If the failure survives step 3, please paste the checker's `Diagnostic information:` block (`IDF_PYTHON_ENV_PATH`, `Python interpreter used`), plus `idf.py --version`, `python -V` and the exact command you ran; that separates "wrong `$IDF_PATH` exported" from "pip writing to a different interpreter".

Full reproduction and evidence: [work record](https://github.com/m5agent/agent-work-logs/blob/c20d5281610228487e59c9b7c9cfa74a147d0595/records/m5stack-github/2026-11-23-cardputer-userdemo-issue-48-idf-python-env/README.md)

The documentation says to use v5.4.2
When I tried that there were other libraries that weren't installed.
Please update to the latest version of tools.

**Conclusion: for Cardputer ADV the doc is right — that branch pins ESP-IDF v5.4.2 — and the "libraries" it is missing are most likely the five components that the branch does not ship; `fetch_repos.py` clones them, ESP-IDF does not install them.**

My earlier v4.4.6 statement applies to `main` (original Cardputer). The ADV path runs through the `CardputerADV` branch: its `README.md:15` says **ESP-IDF v5.4.2** and `dependencies.lock:57` pins `idf: 5.4.2`. The Cardputer ADV docs page links to that branch, so there is no version conflict unless you cloned `main` while reading the ADV page. `git branch --show-current` will tell you which case you are in.

The branch pulls libraries from two places:

1. **Git components that are not committed to the branch.** `repos.json:1-27` lists five repositories cloned into `components/` by `python3 ./fetch_repos.py` (`README.md:7-11`): M5GFX `0.2.15`, M5Unified `0.2.10`, mooncake `v2.2.0`, mooncake_log `v1.3.0`, smooth_ui_toolkit `v2.4.0`. Since `components/` is absent from the branch tree, `idf.py build` before this step cannot resolve those components. From the repo root:

```bash
python3 ./fetch_repos.py
ls components    # expect M5GFX M5Unified mooncake mooncake_log smooth_ui_toolkit
```

2. **IDF-managed components** downloaded from components.espressif.com during configuration (esp-now, esp_tinyusb, tinyusb, radiolib, cmake_utilities in `dependencies.lock`). If the error names one of these, it is a registry/network failure, not a toolchain-version problem.

If the missing items are Python packages (`check_python_dependencies.py`), that is the per-IDF-environment issue from my previous comment: 5.4.2's `install.sh`/`export.sh` must come from the 5.4.2 checkout, and the shell must not still have 6.1's environment exported.

On "update to the latest version of tools": the 5.4.2 pin is a repository-level toolchain choice, not a local dependency. Changing it is a maintainer-owned port plus a full build/hardware re-validation, it is not something an issue reply can do, and it would not install the missing components. It is also not needed to get past this step.

**Evidence level: code-level verification.** `CardputerADV@9d71903`: `README.md:7-15`, `repos.json:1-27`, `fetch_repos.py` (`fetch_dependencies()`), `dependencies.lock:57` and its component list; the branch tree contains no `components/`. No virtual-device or hardware validation applies: the failure is in dependency setup, before any firmware exists.

**Not covered:** I did not run the clone and build (no 5.4.2 toolchain in this session), and I cannot name the missing libraries from the description. If it still fails after step 1, paste the exact command and the first ~20 lines of the error, plus `idf.py --version`, `echo "$IDF_PATH"`, `echo "$IDF_PYTHON_ENV_PATH"`, `python -V`, and `git branch --show-current`.

Building from source shouldn't involve changing the tools from within the source.
The project should build using the latest version of the tools. If that's not the case, then you need to include the tools necessary to successfully build the project.
